what_happened: The job was meant to fix the throughput figures: the landing time, the time spent, and the stated bases. It was rejected at the final verdict. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: the new status.rs test must use fixture records for a landed job with a CI wait and a rebuild, and must show the landing stage covers that duration. There were four blocker or major findings. (1) Blocker: `landing_end` is extended only by host refusal records, not by the landing record the user named, so the landing-and-rebuild figure is still wrong for every ordinary landing. (2) Major: the test uses a 405 host refusal as a stand-in for the CI wait and rebuild, so it passes without testing the requested behavior. (3) Major: the printed basis, the CHANGELOG and the throughput prompt say the CI wait and rebuild have no record, but a landing record exists. (4) Major: the reading does not match the request. No failed checks are listed. The other 6 criteria were met.
cause: Nothing compares the accepted reading with the request's own words before the producer runs. The user named a specific record (the landing record) as the end of the landing stage. The reading substituted a different one (host refusal records), and the criteria were written against that reading. The test fixture also used a stand-in event instead of the records the real writers produce. So the criteria could pass without the request being met. Only the verifier at the final verdict checks the reading against the request, and there rejection is the only outcome. The user's phrase was never resolved against the record types the code actually writes. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the reading.
prevention: Before the producer runs, check the reading in code. Every record type, field or code location the request names must be listed in the reading and resolved to a real writer in the repo. The reading's criteria must then name that record, not a substitute. For a figure built from records, require that the test fixture be made of the records the real writer produces (the landing record with a CI wait and rebuild), and reject fixtures that use another record type as a stand-in. Add a critic check that restates the request's named record in the reading and flags any mismatch before the producer is dispatched.
proposed_request:
Fix the landing-time figure in the throughput status so it is measured to the landing record. Outcome: for an ordinary landed job, the landing stage in `athena status` throughput runs from the verifier's outcome to the landing record, so it covers the CI wait and the rebuild. It must not depend on host refusal records. Acceptance:
- A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixture records of the kinds the real landing writer produces: a landed job with a landing record, a CI wait and a rebuild, and no host refusal record. Running `cargo test -p athena-core status` shows the landing stage duration covers the wait and the rebuild.
- A second test shows a job with no landing record still reports a sensible landing figure and states why.
- The printed basis in Throughput::text, the throughput prompt in hestia.rs and the CHANGELOG say the CI wait and rebuild are measured from the landing record, and no longer say they have no record.
- Before coding, the reading must name the landing record type and where it is written, and confirm it exists in the current snapshot.
